item.title: Escambia County voting surges ahead of Election Day
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Early voting in Escambia County is tracking at about 32 percent as of Monday, with thousands of Florida voters already casting ballots before polls open statewide Tuesday for the midterm elections. Across Florida, nearly 40 percent of registered voters have already participated in early voting or requested mail-in ballots ahead of Election Day,…
item.content:encoded:
Early voting in Escambia County is tracking at about 32 percent as of Monday, with thousands of Florida voters already casting ballots before polls open statewide Tuesday for the midterm elections.

Across Florida, nearly 40 percent of registered voters have already participated in early voting or requested mail-in ballots ahead of Election Day, according to reports from North Escambia. The strong early turnout suggests robust participation in this year's midterm contests.

Escambia County voters can cast ballots at their regular polling locations Tuesday, or those who haven't already voted early can visit their designated precinct on Election Day. Poll locations open at 7 a.m. and close at 7 p.m.

item.content:encoded:
Professional women's softball is coming to downtown Pensacola. The Florida Vibe, a franchise in the Professional Softball League (PSL), will call Blue Wahoos Stadium home starting in 2027, according to North Escambia.

The community is invited to welcome the new team during a public ceremony at the stadium on Monday, November 16, at 5:00 p.m. The event will mark an official introduction of the franchise to the Pensacola area.

The addition of the Florida Vibe expands professional sports offerings in the region and adds another tenant to Blue Wahoos Stadium, which currently hosts the Pensacola Blue Wahoos minor league baseball team.

item.title: High School Football Makeup Games Continue Tonight and Wednesday
item.dc:creator: newsroom

Tuesday night's matchups include Navarre at Tate, Gulf Breeze at Escambia, Washington at Milton, Pine Forest at Pensacola, and South Walton at West Florida. Wednesday's slate features Northview at…
item.content:encoded:
Area high schools are wrapping up their regular season with makeup games this week after Hurricane Isaias forced postponements earlier in the fall.

Tuesday night's matchups include Navarre at Tate, Gulf Breeze at Escambia, Washington at Milton, Pine Forest at Pensacola, and South Walton at West Florida.

Wednesday's slate features Northview at Blountstown, Pace at Niceville, and Jay at Marianna. These games represent the final regular-season action for most area programs before the postseason gets underway.

item.title: Warm Tuesday Before Rain and Cool-Down Wednesday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola-area residents can expect pleasant conditions today with highs climbing near 80 degrees, but a weather system moving through will bring increasing shower chances this afternoon and widespread rain overnight into Wednesday, according to the National Weather Service. The most significant rain activity is expected Tuesday night through…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola-area residents can expect pleasant conditions today with highs climbing near 80 degrees, but a weather system moving through will bring increasing shower chances this afternoon and widespread rain overnight into Wednesday, according to the National Weather Service.

The most significant rain activity is expected Tuesday night through Wednesday morning as the system pushes through Northwest Florida. Thunderstorms are likely during that window, so residents should be prepared for wet conditions if heading to the polls today.

Once the system clears, skies will improve and a noticeable cooling trend takes hold as we head toward the weekend, bringing more seasonal fall temperatures back to the area.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County voters head to the polls today, Tuesday, November 3, for Election Day. Polling places across the county are open and accepting ballots for local, state, and federal races.

According to NorthEscambia.com, election results will begin posting to their Facebook page shortly after polls close this evening. Complete local and state results are expected to be available on their website and social media channels Wednesday morning.

If you haven't voted yet, check your voter registration status and polling location at your county supervisor of elections office or online voter portal.

The alleged scheme involved repeated fraudulent transactions, with the suspect accused of misusing the…
item.content:encoded:
A Cantonment resident is facing felony charges after investigators say he used a company fuel card to make nearly 200 unauthorized gas purchases for his personal vehicle over approximately 20 months, according to reporting from North Escambia.

The alleged scheme involved repeated fraudulent transactions, with the suspect accused of misusing the card entrusted to him for legitimate business purposes. The investigation focused on the pattern of unauthorized activity spanning the extended period.

Details on the specific employer, exact dollar amount of losses, or the timeline of the investigation were not immediately available. The case has been referred for prosecution.

item.title: Gulf Shores moves to restore local control of Fat Tuesday parade

The move comes as the Alabama coastal city seeks to reinvigorate its Mardi Gras tradition through a new partnership structure that gives community organizations greater…
item.content:encoded: After months of negotiation, Gulf Shores city leaders are working toward an agreement that would return the city's Fat Tuesday parade to local krewes, according to WKRG News 5. The move comes as the Alabama coastal city seeks to reinvigorate its Mardi Gras tradition through a new partnership structure that gives community organizations greater oversight of the longtime celebration. Details of the agreement remain in development, but the shift represents an effort to preserve the parade while distributing responsibility among local groups rather than maintaining centralized city management.

item.title: Northwest Florida surpasses 151,000 early votes as midterm election arrives today
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: As voters head to the polls today for the 2026 midterm election, Northwest Florida has already seen substantial early voting turnout across the region. According to WKRG News 5, roughly 151,000 residents in Escambia, Santa Rosa, and Okaloosa counties cast early ballots ahead of Election Day. The strong early voting numbers suggest significant…
item.content:encoded:
As voters head to the polls today for the 2026 midterm election, Northwest Florida has already seen substantial early voting turnout across the region. According to WKRG News 5, roughly 151,000 residents in Escambia, Santa Rosa, and Okaloosa counties cast early ballots ahead of Election Day.

The strong early voting numbers suggest significant voter engagement in the region as candidates and ballot measures compete for support. Election officials across the three-county area have been processing votes throughout the early voting period to prepare for today's results.

Voters heading to polls today should bring valid identification and be prepared for potential wait times, depending on their precinct. Local election supervisors have stressed the importance of voting on Election Day if early voting deadlines have passed, with polls typically open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. in most Florida precincts.

item.title: Escambia County voters head to polls today; check your location first
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County residents are voting in the November 3rd General Election today, and the Supervisor of Elections office is reminding voters to confirm their polling place before heading out. Voters can find their assigned precinct on their sample ballot, voter information card, or online at EscambiaVotes.gov. The elections office also notes that…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County residents are voting in the November 3rd General Election today, and the Supervisor of Elections office is reminding voters to confirm their polling place before heading out.

Voters can find their assigned precinct on their sample ballot, voter information card, or online at EscambiaVotes.gov. The elections office also notes that several polling locations have changed for 2026—three precincts are temporarily relocated this year, and voters in those areas were notified by mail at least two weeks ago. Precinct 14 has moved to Pensacola Main Library on North Spring Street; Precinct 35 is now at Heights Baptist Church on Pickens Avenue; and Precinct 70 is at The Gathering Place at Pensacola Christian College.

Voters must bring a photo and signature ID—one of 12 approved forms—or risk receiving a provisional ballot. Those who requested a Vote-by-Mail ballot but haven't returned it can still vote in person at their polling place. Anyone with an unreturned mail ballot should bring the package to the polls, though it's not required. Completed Vote-by-Mail ballots must be returned to the Supervisor of Elections office by 7 p.m. today; they cannot be dropped at individual precincts.

For questions, voters can call the Supervisor of Elections at (850) 595-3900, email soe@escambiavotes.gov, or visit EscambiaVotes.gov.

item.title: SEC Women's Soccer Tournament Returns to Pensacola Nov. 8–15
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County will host the Southeastern Conference Women's Soccer Tournament for the fifth consecutive year, with matches running November 8–15 at Ashton Brosnaham Athletic Park. The week-long event will feature the top 12 women's soccer teams competing for the conference championship. The tournament has become a significant draw for the region…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County will host the Southeastern Conference Women's Soccer Tournament for the fifth consecutive year, with matches running November 8–15 at Ashton Brosnaham Athletic Park. The week-long event will feature the top 12 women's soccer teams competing for the conference championship.

The tournament has become a significant draw for the region since 2022, bringing thousands of visitors and generating millions in local economic impact. District 5 Commissioner Steven Barry called the event "an exciting opportunity" to showcase Escambia County and Northwest Florida as a destination for major sporting events. The county's partnership with Pensacola Sports and the SEC has made the annual tournament possible.

Parks and Recreation Director Michael Rhodes said the county has completed facility improvements at Ashton Brosnaham to meet SEC standards. "Our team has been hard at work to ensure the field is ready to welcome the players and their fans," Rhodes said. Fans can view the official tournament bracket, purchase tickets, and check the game schedule on the SEC website and Pensacola Sports website.

item.title: Shrimp Basket closes Pensacola location as chain consolidates

The closure is part of a broader consolidation by parent company Artistry Restaurants, which shut down six locations across Alabama and Florida, including a Bay Minette, Alabama outpost. Sunday, November 1st was the last day of business for the Pensacola restaurant. The…
item.content:encoded: The Pensacola Shrimp Basket has closed its doors, according to WKRG News 5. The closure is part of a broader consolidation by parent company Artistry Restaurants, which shut down six locations across Alabama and Florida, including a Bay Minette, Alabama outpost. Sunday, November 1st was the last day of business for the Pensacola restaurant. The company has not publicly disclosed details about the reasons for the closures or whether other Shrimp Basket locations will continue operating in the region. Shrimp Basket has been a fixture in the casual dining scene across the Gulf Coast for years, known for its seafood offerings.

item.title: Santa Rosa County phone outage hits multiple government offices
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County residents encountered difficulty reaching several county offices by phone Monday after incoming calls went down across multiple departments, according to officials. AT&T is aware of the outage and working on repairs, Santa Rosa County Communications & Media Relations said in a statement issued at 1:20 p.m. The disruption affected…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County residents encountered difficulty reaching several county offices by phone Monday after incoming calls went down across multiple departments, according to officials.

AT&T is aware of the outage and working on repairs, Santa Rosa County Communications & Media Relations said in a statement issued at 1:20 p.m. The disruption affected Engineering, Environmental Department, Housing, Inspections & Permits, Planning & Zoning, Mosquito Control, Public Works, and Veterans Services.

Until phone service is restored, the county is directing residents to use email and online channels. Engineering, Environmental, Housing, and other departments have published email addresses for inquiries, while permit and planning applications can be submitted through My Government Online at mgoconnect.org. Public Works work order requests are available through SeeClickFix, and residents can book Veterans Services appointments online. The county said it will issue an update when repairs are complete.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Hosts Drive-Through Rabies Vaccination Clinic Nov. 13
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County will offer a quick, affordable way for pet owners to keep their animals protected against rabies later this month. On Friday, November 13, from 4 to 6 p.m., DOH-Santa Rosa will run a drive-through rabies vaccination clinic at Pensacola State College's Milton Campus, 5988 Highway 90. Pet owners…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County will offer a quick, affordable way for pet owners to keep their animals protected against rabies later this month.

On Friday, November 13, from 4 to 6 p.m., DOH-Santa Rosa will run a drive-through rabies vaccination clinic at Pensacola State College's Milton Campus, 5988 Highway 90. Pet owners can stay in their vehicles while veterinarians from The Ark Animal Hospital administer shots for just $10 per animal—cash and checks only. A valid driver's license is required for check payments. Pets must be secured in a vehicle, crate, or on leash.

Each vaccinated animal will receive a certificate and rabies tag. The clinic is expected to vaccinate between 200 and 300 dogs and cats. According to DOH-Santa Rosa Health Administrator R. Matthew Dobson, the partnership with local veterinarians aims to make rabies prevention more accessible to the community. "These clinics bring a needed service in a more accessible way," Dobson said.

Rabies remains fatal once symptoms appear but is entirely preventable through vaccination. The health department urges pet owners to keep animals supervised, avoid contact with wildlife, and report any bites or scratches to Santa Rosa Animal Control at 850-983-4680 or DOH-Santa Rosa at 850-983-5200. For questions about the clinic, call 850-564-2278.

Details about the circumstances leading to the shooting and the condition of the vehicle's occupants were not immediately clear. The case remains under investigation by the Sheriff's Office.

item.title: Florida Democrats' Final Ad Targets 30 Years of GOP Control Before Election
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Democratic Party released its closing argument ad Monday ahead of Election Day, with party chair Nikki Fried criticizing three decades of Republican control and Florida's affordability crisis. The digital ad, which is running statewide, features Fried rallying volunteers at a canvass launch and echoing concerns voters have raised about…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Democratic Party released its closing argument ad Monday ahead of Election Day, with party chair Nikki Fried criticizing three decades of Republican control and Florida's affordability crisis. The digital ad, which is running statewide, features Fried rallying volunteers at a canvass launch and echoing concerns voters have raised about housing costs and economic pressures.

In the ad, Fried argues that Republican leadership in Tallahassee has resulted in an affordability crisis pricing families out of their communities, rising insurance premiums, and cuts to public schools. "Floridians are tired of paying the price for Republican failures," Fried said in a statement. "Tomorrow, we have a chance to say enough is enough. We deserve better, and we deserve leaders who will finally put Florida families first."

The ad is running on digital platforms across Florida in English as Democrats make their final pitch to voters before the polls open Tuesday.

item.title: FEMA Registration Points Now Open in Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Federal Emergency Management Agency registration points have opened across the region to help residents apply for Individual Assistance following Hurricane Isaias. In Escambia County, three registration points are operating from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. today through Wednesday at Bayview Senior Center (2000 E. Lloyd St.), Escambia County Central Office…
item.content:encoded:
Federal Emergency Management Agency registration points have opened across the region to help residents apply for Individual Assistance following Hurricane Isaias.

In Escambia County, three registration points are operating from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. today through Wednesday at Bayview Senior Center (2000 E. Lloyd St.), Escambia County Central Office Complex (3363 W. Park Place), and Cokesbury Church (5725 N. 9th Ave.). Starting Monday, Nov. 2, hours expand to 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. through Nov. 4.

Santa Rosa County has opened two permanent registration points at the Santa Rosa County Administrative Complex in Milton (6495 Caroline Street, Suite L hallway) and Bray-Hendricks Park in Jay (5259 Booker Lane). Both locations operate Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., with additional locations and weekend hours possible as recovery efforts continue. State Emergency Response Team staff will be available at all sites.

Eligible residents can apply for grants covering temporary housing, home repairs, and other disaster-related needs. Applicants can register online at DisasterAssistance.gov, call the FEMA Helpline at 1-800-621-3362 (TTY 1-800-462-7585, open 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily), or use the FEMA mobile app. County officials recommend filing insurance claims before applying for federal assistance.

item.content:encoded:
Organizers of the Sand in My Boots beach festival have announced the 2027 lineup, with country star Morgan Wallen set to headline the three-day event. The festival is scheduled for May 21–23 on the beach in Gulf Shores, Alabama, according to a news release reported by WKRG News 5.

Sand in My Boots has become a popular spring destination for music fans across the Gulf Coast region. More details about additional performers and event logistics are expected to be released in the coming weeks.
